metaDescription: Six lawn mowers under $200: 144cc gas push mowers from 18 to 20 inches plus corded and cordless electrics, compared on engines, decks and upkeep.
expertTake: The SENIX 20-inch 144cc gas mower is the best overall for deck width and the ability to handle overgrown grass. The LawnMaster MEB1216K corded 16-inch is the value pick for a small lawn near an outlet. Anyone with a lot of slopes should skip push mowers and pay for self-propel.
introParagraphs: This is the price point where gas push mowers first appear alongside electrics. A small four-stroke engine gives you unlimited runtime and the ability to chew through tall grass, at the cost of fuel, oil and noise that electrics avoid. Gas wins on grass height, electric wins on convenience.

The cap here is $200, and prices move, so it reflects listing prices when this guide was updated. The choice is less about which mower is best and more about which energy source fits your lawn, your storage and your patience for upkeep.

products.name: SENIX 20-Inch 144cc 4-Cycle Gas Push Lawn Mower
products.description:
The SENIX 20-inch pairs a 144cc four-cycle engine with a 20-inch deck, the widest cutting path in this lineup. A four-cycle engine runs on plain gasoline with oil in a separate sump, unlike a two-stroke that needs mixed fuel, so it is cleaner and easier to live with. The listing says it handles overgrown grass and weeds and works on flat lawns and slopes, which is the real advantage of a gas mower over a small electric.

A 144cc engine delivers roughly three horsepower of gross output, and gross ratings overstate real net power, so treat it as a capable but not strong engine. Against the 18-inch SENIX it adds two inches of width, and against the electrics it has no runtime limit. A slim body suits narrow side yards and dog runs.

Ownership is where gas differs. Change the oil once a season, replace the spark plug and air filter each year, and run the carburetor dry or add stabilizer before winter storage. Expect to pull a recoil starter. It is the choice for anyone who needs to cut tall, thick grass without worrying about a battery. Before the first start, check the oil level, because many gas mowers ship with the sump empty to prevent shipping leaks.
products.bestFor: Medium lawns with tall or neglected grass where unlimited runtime matters.
pros: 20 inch deck is the widest in the group
144cc four-cycle engine runs on plain gasoline
No runtime limit like a battery mower
Slim body fits narrow side yards
cons: Needs yearly oil, plug and filter service

products.name: SENIX 18-Inch 144cc Gas Lawn Mower, 3-Position Height
products.description:
The SENIX 18-inch is the lighter and cheaper sibling of the 20-inch model, with the same 144cc four-cycle engine and a deck two inches narrower. Three height positions span 1.2 to 3.15 inches, coarser than the five and six position levers on rivals but enough for most lawns.

Compared with the PowerSmart 18-inch, it matches the deck and engine size, so the difference is mostly in fit and finish and the height range. It is marketed as beginner-friendly, and a smaller deck is easier to push and store.

Gas upkeep applies: oil once a season, plug and air filter yearly, and stabilizer before storage. The three-position height lever is the main limitation. Store it with the handle folded and the fuel stabilized, and the engine should start on the second or third pull. Over three seasons the throttle cable and the wheel hardware are the wear points worth a glance each spring.
products.bestFor: Smaller lawns and first-time gas mower owners.
pros: Wide height range of 1.2 to 3.15 inches

products.name: PowerSmart EasyCut 18-Inch 144cc Gas Lawn Mower
products.description:
The PowerSmart EasyCut uses a 144cc four-stroke overhead-valve engine, an 18-inch steel deck and side discharge. Side discharge throws clippings out the side so you can keep moving through tall, thick grass without clogging a bag.

A steel deck is more robust than plastic and survives rocks and stumps, though it can rust if left wet. An OHV engine is generally more efficient and quieter than a side-valve design.

Against the SENIX it matches engine and deck, so the choice is brand and feature mix. It has no bag in the description, so plan on side discharge only. Change the oil seasonally and keep the underside clean. Rinse and dry the deck after each cut to slow rust. Wet clippings can pack the discharge chute, so mow when the grass is dry for the cleanest result.
products.bestFor: Tall, thick grass where side discharge keeps the deck from clogging.
cons: No bag described, so clippings stay on the lawn
Steel deck can rust if left wet

products.name: LawnMaster MEB1216K 12A Corded Electric Mower, 16-Inch
products.description:
The LawnMaster MEB1216K is a 12-amp corded mower at 3,500 RPM with a 16-inch deck and five cutting heights. Twelve amps is about 1,400 watts, more than the 11-amp corded models, and 3,500 RPM gives a fast blade tip.

It has no fuel, oil or battery to manage, and it starts at the push of a button. The cost is the cord, which must be managed carefully behind you, and a 14 AWG extension is the right match for 12 amps.

Against the gas mowers it is quieter and cheaper to run but limited to areas near an outlet. LawnMaster has decades of parts support, which is a real advantage. There is no fuel to stale, which makes it the easiest mower here to leave in a shed. If you only mow a small area, a gas engine would be overkill, and the quiet of this mower is a bonus.
products.bestFor: Small lawns near an outlet where quiet and no upkeep matter.
cons: Smaller deck than the gas models

products.name: EWORK 40V 14-Inch Cordless Mower, Two 4.0Ah Batteries
products.description:
The EWORK is a complete cordless kit with two 20V 4.0Ah batteries and a fast charger, an all-copper motor reaching 3,800 RPM and a 14-inch deck. The listing says it cuts thick, tangled grass, which is a claim worth tempering because a 14-inch electric mower does not match a gas engine in tall growth.

It is lightweight and quiet, and the two-battery kit gives you flexibility. Against the 17-inch cordless in the cheaper tier it has a narrower deck, so this is the pick only if you want the EWORK kit contents.

Charge the packs after use and keep them indoors. Charge both packs after each cut so the next job starts full. Because it is light, the EWORK is easy for a teenager or an older owner to handle.
products.bestFor: Small lawns where a light cordless kit is wanted.
pros: 14 inch deck is easy to maneuver
cons: Tall thick grass is hard for a small electric

products.name: 17-Inch Brushless Cordless Mower, Two 20V 4.0Ah, 50L Bag
products.description:
This cordless mower has a 17-inch deck, a brushless 3,000 RPM motor, six heights from 1 to 3 inches and a 50-liter bag. Two 20V 4.0Ah batteries power it.

It is the widest cordless deck in this lineup, but it still trails the 20-inch gas mower by three inches. Against the EWORK it has three more inches and a brushless motor.

The batteries are the wear item. Buy a spare early and store them indoors. At year three the batteries are the expected wear item, so buy a spare early. Compared with the SENIX 20-inch, you trade three inches of width and unlimited runtime for silence and zero fuel handling.
products.bestFor: Cordless owners who want the widest electric deck at this price.
pros: 17 inch deck is wide for a cordless
cons: Peak watt figure is not sustained output

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 144cc gas engine gives unlimited runtime and handles tall grass, but needs oil, plugs and fuel stabilizer. An electric mower starts instantly and needs almost nothing, but is limited by cord or battery. For lawns over a tenth of an acre with thick growth, gas is the safer choice. Electric mowers also avoid the noise that annoys neighbors on weekend mornings. Many owners who start with electric move to gas as their lawn or ambitions grow, and the reverse also happens.

A 144cc engine is a small displacement: gross power ratings run around three horsepower but net output is lower. Compare engine type instead: a four-stroke OHV is cleaner than an older design. Cubic centimeters alone do not guarantee cutting power. A bigger number is not a guarantee: blade design and deck shape decide how well it cuts. Look for an auto-choke and a primer bulb if you dislike fiddly starts.

A 20-inch deck covers 11 percent more than 18 inches and 43 percent more than 14 inches. Wider decks mean fewer passes but are harder to turn in tight yards. Measure the gate before you buy. Measure the gate and the narrowest path on your lawn before choosing. A narrow deck does a cleaner job around trees and beds.

Side discharge, as on the PowerSmart, suits tall grass but leaves clippings on the lawn. Bags tidy but add weight. A 50-liter bag on the 17-inch cordless fills fast in thick grass. Mulching every second cut cuts the number of bag stops. A closed mulching deck with a sharp blade cuts clippings fine enough to vanish.

The SENIX 18-inch offers three positions from 1.2 to 3.15 inches, while the cordless offers six from 1 to 3 inches. More positions mean finer control, which matters when cutting grass short in stages. Raise the deck in dry summer weather to protect the turf. Use the highest setting for the first cut of spring.

Gasoline goes stale in about a month. Add stabilizer or run the carburetor dry before storing. Electric mowers avoid this, which is a major reason owners choose them. Ethanol-free fuel keeps carburetors cleaner for longer. Fuel containers should be stored away from living spaces.

howWeEvaluated.title: Engine and power
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared engine type and size. Four-stroke 144cc engines scored well for runtime, electrics for convenience. We did not give extra credit to claimed horsepower figures.

howWeEvaluated.title: Deck and cut
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared decks from 14 to 20 inches and heights from three to six positions. Height ranges were compared directly from the listings. Deck width and height steps were treated as separate scores.

howWeEvaluated.title: Upkeep
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed oil, plug and fuel needs for gas against zero-upkeep electrics. Upkeep costs were estimated from standard service intervals.

howWeEvaluated.title: Grass handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We credited side discharge for tall grass and bags for tidy lawns. Discharge and bag options were compared from listing descriptions.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated patterns on hard starts, stale fuel and fading batteries. Hard-start complaints on gas mowers shaped the maintenance advice.

cards.label: Gas
cards.text: The SENIX pair and PowerSmart give unlimited runtime and handle tall grass, but need oil, plugs and stabilizer.

cards.label: Electric
cards.text: The LawnMaster, EWORK and 17-inch cordless start instantly and need almost no upkeep, but are limited by cord or battery.

howToChoose.note: Pick gas for large or tall lawns, electric for small tidy ones.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A four-stroke engine, side discharge and a steel deck. Raise the height and cut twice.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The SENIX 20-inch and PowerSmart 18-inch are the two best fits.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have slopes or more than a quarter acre, which calls for self-propel.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your lawn is small and near an outlet, where the LawnMaster suffices.

maintenance.why: Old oil loses protection. Warm the engine first and drain fully. Run the engine until warm before draining the oil.

maintenance.task: Replace spark plug and air filter
maintenance.why: A fouled plug causes hard starts. Gap the new plug to the manual's spec.
Stale gasoline gums the carburetor. Add stabilizer before the final fill of the season.
A dull blade tears grass and strains the engine. Mark the blade's original angle before you sharpen it.
Caked clippings restrict airflow and rust steel decks. Scrape the deck with a plastic scraper, never your hand.

faq.a: For a typical suburban lawn, yes. For slopes or half-acre lots, a self-propelled mower with a bigger engine is better. A tune-up each spring keeps a small gas engine happy. Older engines are happier with this routine than newer ones.

faq.q: Should I buy gas or electric?
faq.a: Gas for tall grass and larger lawns, electric for small tidy ones and for low upkeep. Electric mowers shine on small lawns. The best mower is the one that fits the lawn you actually have.

Gas push mowers with 144cc engines and cordless or corded electrics. Prices move and the cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated. Electric mowers cost little to run but can be limited by the cord or pack. Check that the listed price is still below the cap before ordering.

faq.q: How do I store a gas mower?
faq.a: Add stabilizer or run the carburetor dry, change the oil and store it level. Run the carburetor dry or add stabilizer.

faq.q: Do I need to mix oil with gas?
faq.a: No on a four-cycle engine. Oil goes in a separate sump. Use fresh 87 octane gasoline in four-cycle mowers.

Most lawns do well at two and a half to three inches. Never remove more than a third at once. Cut when the grass is dry for the cleanest result. Mow when dry to avoid clumping and keep the blade clean.
